title: A Belt, a Cloudy Liquid, a Melted Chocolate Bar: Three Quiet Inventors
title_zh: 一条安全带、一杯浑液、一块融化的巧克力：三位安静改变世界的发明家
intro_zh: 本文约526词，含6个CET-4核心词（patent、claim、flexible、household、ordinary、transform），句子难度中等，理解目标85%-90%。

paragraphs.en: Ask anyone to name a great inventor and you will probably hear the same names: Thomas Edison, the Wright brothers, Alexander Graham Bell. Yet many of the people who quietly changed our daily lives never became famous at all. Their stories are less about genius and more about noticing a small problem and refusing to leave it alone.
paragraphs.zh: 随便问一个人最伟大的发明家是谁，你大概会听到那几个熟悉的名字：托马斯·爱迪生、莱特兄弟、亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔。然而，许多悄悄改变了我们日常生活的人，却从未出名。他们的故事与其说关乎天才，不如说关乎注意到一个小问题，并且不肯对它置之不理。

paragraphs.en: In 1959, a Swedish engineer named Nils Bohlin was working for the car company Volvo. At that time, road crashes were claiming thousands of lives every year in Europe alone. Most seat belts had only two points and could even injure the people they were supposed to protect. Bohlin spent months studying how the human body moves during an accident, and he finally designed the three-point belt that is still used in cars today.
paragraphs.zh: 1959年，一位名叫尼尔斯·博林的瑞典工程师在沃尔沃汽车公司工作。当时，仅在欧洲，交通事故每年就夺去数千人的生命。大多数安全带只有两个固定点，甚至可能伤害它们本该保护的人。博林花了几个月研究人在事故中身体的运动方式，最终设计出三点式安全带——这种安全带至今仍用在汽车上。

paragraphs.en: Volvo could have kept the patent and earned a fortune. Instead, the company opened the design to every car maker for free. The result is hard to imagine today: the three-point belt has saved well over one million lives, and it is now required in almost every country on Earth. One quiet decision did more good than any advertisement ever could.
paragraphs.zh: 沃尔沃本可以保留专利、大赚一笔。但公司反而把这项设计免费开放给了所有汽车制造商。结果在今天简直难以想象：三点式安全带已挽救了一百多万人的生命，如今世界上几乎所有国家都要求使用它。一个安静的决定，比任何广告起的作用都大。

paragraphs.en: Stephanie Kwolek's story is similar. In 1965, this American chemist was looking for a light material to put inside car tires. One day she produced a strange, cloudy liquid that at first seemed useless. Instead of throwing it away, she tested it carefully. The liquid turned out to be surprisingly flexible, and once it dried it was five times stronger than steel of the same weight.
paragraphs.zh: 斯蒂芬妮·克沃勒克的故事很相似。1965年，这位美国化学家正在寻找一种用来做汽车轮胎的轻质材料。有一天，她做出了一种奇怪的浑浊液体，起初看起来毫无用处。她没有把它倒掉，而是仔细地对它做了测试。这种液体竟然出奇地柔韧，干燥后的强度是同重量钢材的五倍。

paragraphs.en: That material became Kevlar. Today it protects police officers, soldiers and firefighters, and it is used in helmets, gloves and even bridge cables. Kwolek never expected her work to save lives — she was only trying to save fuel for drivers. Her name is not on the tip of everyone's tongue, but her material is quietly holding things together. She later said that a good scientist must be curious first and patient second.
paragraphs.zh: 这种材料后来成了凯夫拉。今天，它保护着警察、士兵和消防员，还被用在头盔、手套乃至桥梁缆索上。克沃勒克从没指望自己的工作能救命——她只是想让司机省点油。她的名字并不为人熟知，但她的材料正默默地把许多东西牢牢撑住。她后来说，一个优秀的科学家首先要有好奇心，其次要有耐心。

paragraphs.en: Then there is Percy Spencer, an engineer who worked with radar equipment in the 1940s. One afternoon, standing beside a machine, he noticed that the chocolate bar in his pocket had melted. Curious, he placed some popcorn near the machine and watched the kernels pop one by one. Without planning to, he had discovered a completely new way to heat food.
paragraphs.zh: 还有珀西·斯宾塞，一位在20世纪40年代从事雷达设备研究的工程师。一天下午，他站在一台机器旁边，发现口袋里的巧克力棒融化了。出于好奇，他把一些玉米粒放在机器旁，看着它们一颗颗爆开。在完全没有计划的情况下，他发现了一种全新的加热食物的方式。

paragraphs.en: The first microwave oven, sold in 1947, was as tall as a person and cost about as much as a small car. Few families could imagine owning one. Yet engineers kept making the device smaller and cheaper, and today more than nine out of ten American households have a microwave in the kitchen. A job that once took an hour now takes about three minutes.
paragraphs.zh: 1947年出售的第一台微波炉有一人高，价格大约相当于一辆小汽车。很少有家庭能想象自己拥有一台。但工程师们不断把这个装置做得更小、更便宜，如今超过十分之九的美国家庭厨房里都有一台微波炉。过去要花一小时的事情，现在大约三分钟就能完成。

paragraphs.en: What connects these three inventors? None of them set out to become famous. They paid close attention to small, ordinary things: a seat belt, a cloudy liquid, a melting chocolate bar. And at least one of them chose to share the reward instead of protecting it. Perhaps that is the real lesson. The world is often transformed by people who simply refuse to accept that this is how it has always been.
paragraphs.zh: 这三位发明家之间有什么共同点？他们中没有人一开始就想着出名。他们都密切关注那些普通的小东西：一条安全带、一杯浑液、一块融化的巧克力。而且至少其中一人选择分享回报，而不是把它护在手里。也许这才是真正的启示：世界常常是被那些干脆拒绝接受“事情本来就是这样”的人所改变的。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Famous inventors like Edison deserve far more public attention.
Quiet inventors who noticed small problems have greatly changed daily life.
Car safety is the most important field of invention in history.
Most useful inventions were discovered completely by accident.
questions.explain: 全文围绕三位并不出名的发明家展开：他们关注身边的小问题，其成果（安全带、凯夫拉、微波炉）深刻改变了日常生活，故B正确。A与文章相反；C、D只是文中个别细节，不能概括主旨。

questions.q: According to the passage, what did Volvo do with Bohlin's three-point belt?
options: It sold the patent to other companies at a high price.
It kept the design secret for many years.
It opened the design to all car makers without charge.
It used the belt only in cars sold in Sweden.
questions.explain: 第三段明确说沃尔沃本可以保留专利赚钱，却“opened the design to every car maker for free”，即免费向所有汽车厂商开放设计，故选C。A、B与原文相反，D文中无据。

questions.q: What can be inferred about Stephanie Kwolek from the passage?
options: She created Kevlar mainly in order to save people's lives.
She threw the cloudy liquid away before testing it.
She became rich and famous soon after her discovery.
She did not plan to produce a life-saving material.
questions.explain: 第四、五段指出她的目标是寻找轻质轮胎材料、帮司机省油，从未指望救人，因此可推断她并非有意发明救命材料，D正确。A与原文相反；B、C文中均无依据（她做了测试，且名声并不广）。

questions.q: The word "claiming" in Paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to _____.
questions.explain: “crashes were claiming thousands of lives”意为交通事故“夺去”数千人的生命，claim在此等于take (lives)，故选A。demand（要求）、state（陈述）、ask for（请求）均不符合语境。
